name: South China Sea confrontation (Philippines vs China)
started: 2023-01-01 (current phase of escalating coast guard confrontations; Scarborough standoff dates to 2012)
summary: China and the Philippines are locked in a non-lethal but physical contest for control of Scarborough Shoal and Second Thomas Shoal, fought with coast guard cutters, water cannon, rammings and boarding confrontations. China's presence at Scarborough hit a record in 2026, and Manila now patrols with US Coast Guard support.

sides.name: Philippines
members: Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR)
backers: United States (treaty ally; joint patrols incl. first US Coast Guard cutter near Scarborough, May 2026)
sides.strength: PCG and BFAR averaged 43 ship-days per month at Scarborough in H1 2026 (AMTI).

sides.name: China
sides.strength: CCG logged 933 ship-days at Scarborough in H1 2026 (156 per month); 6 to 8 militia vessels near-continuously present (AMTI).

background: China took effective control of Scarborough Shoal, about 120 nautical miles from Luzon, after a 2012 standoff, and an international tribunal ruled against its sweeping claims in 2016. At Second Thomas Shoal the Philippines keeps a handful of marines aboard the grounded warship BRP Sierra Madre, and Chinese efforts to block resupply produced violent encounters until a secret provisional arrangement in July 2024.

In fall 2025 China declared a 'national nature reserve' at Scarborough, which Manila sees as a possible precursor to construction, and installed two buoys there in October 2025. This matters because the US-Philippine Mutual Defense Treaty could be invoked if a Philippine public vessel or service member is attacked, making these low-level clashes a potential trigger for a wider US-China crisis.
year: AMTI recorded 933 China Coast Guard ship-days at Scarborough in the first half of 2026, nearly equal to all of 2025 (1,099) and the highest since tracking began in 2019, with CCG ships holding a perimeter about 30 nautical miles out and 112 days of encounters with Philippine vessels. In April 2026 the Philippines accused China of using cyanide around Second Thomas Shoal. On 25 May Philippine authorities found a 6 by 6 metre floating platform inside the Scarborough lagoon, which China called a temporary research facility; it was removed on 17 June. From 26 to 30 May the US cutter Midgett joined Philippine ships for the first US Coast Guard joint patrol near the shoal, and the PLA Southern Theater Command held counter-exercises. On 20 July China Coast Guard personnel struck a Philippine Navy officer with a baton near the Sierra Madre at Second Thomas Shoal, and on 23 July a CCG ship hit a Philippine fisheries vessel with a water cannon at Scarborough while ASEAN foreign ministers met in Manila. In mid-September a CCG vessel struck and damaged the BFAR ship BRP Datu Magat Salamat off Palawan.
situation: As of late October 2026 China maintains a near-permanent cordon around Scarborough and continues to contest Philippine resupply at Second Thomas Shoal. There have been injuries and damaged ships but no deaths. Manila is investigating preliminary reports of Chinese structures at Scarborough, and Beijing warns of 'bitter consequences' if Manila acts with outside support.
technical: CCG ship-days at Scarborough: 516 (2024), 1,099 (2025), 933 (H1 2026); monthly average 156 in H1 2026 vs 90 in H1 2025; May 2026 peak of 216 (AMTI).

CCG perimeter roughly 30 nautical miles from the shoal, with some cutters patrolling along or beyond the nine-dash line to intercept Philippine vessels; 6 to 8 maritime militia vessels keep near-continuous presence closer in (AMTI).
CCG-Philippine interactions on 112 days in H1 2026, about 19 days per month; on 27 May CCG 21563 encountered BRP Datu Pagbuaya (AMTI).
Floating 6 x 6 m platform in the lagoon (25 May to 17 Jun 2026) coincided with research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33; two Chinese buoys installed Oct 2025 remain (AMTI).

First US Coast Guard cutter in a joint patrol near Scarborough: USCGC Midgett (WMSL-757) with BRP Antonio Luna (FFG-14) and BRP Melchora Aquino (MRRV-9702), 26-30 May 2026, about 35 to 40 nm from the shoal (USNI News).
China declared a national nature reserve at Scarborough in fall 2025 (USNI News).
20 Jul 2026: CCG personnel struck a Philippine Navy officer with a baton near BRP Sierra Madre (Wikipedia: 2026 in the Philippines).
23 Jul 2026: CCG water cannon 'indirect hit' on a Philippine fisheries vessel at Scarborough; China said it drove away two Philippine vessels (Reuters via Jakarta Post).
Mid-Sep 2026: CCG vessel struck BFAR's BRP Datu Magat Salamat off Palawan, causing damage (Wikipedia: 2026 in the Philippines).
A US carrier strike group that had spent months in the South China Sea left for the Iran war in 2026 (USNI News).
casualties: No deaths in 2026 incidents found; one Philippine Navy officer injured on 20 Jul 2026 (Wikipedia: 2026 in the Philippines).

timeline.event: China installs two buoys at Scarborough (month per AMTI; day approximate).
Floating Chinese platform found inside Scarborough lagoon (removed 17 Jun).
First US Coast Guard cutter joins Philippine patrol near Scarborough (to 30 May).
CCG personnel strike Philippine Navy officer with baton at Second Thomas Shoal.
CCG water cannon hits Philippine fisheries vessel at Scarborough during ASEAN meetings in Manila.
Reported date of CCG ramming of BRP Datu Magat Salamat off Palawan (listed with mid-September events).

outlook: The key tripwires are any Chinese construction at Scarborough, a death or serious injury in a resupply clash, and the scale of US involvement in patrols. Watch AMTI's second-half 2026 data and Manila's investigation into reported structures.

zones.name: Second Thomas Shoal (Ayungin)
zones.note: BRP Sierra Madre outpost; resupply confrontations incl. 20 Jul 2026 baton clash.

zones.name: West of Palawan
zones.note: Approximate area of the mid-Sep 2026 ramming of BRP Datu Magat Salamat.

battles.name: Water cannon attack at Scarborough Shoal
battles.outcome: Indirect water cannon hit; China said it drove away two Philippine vessels.
battles.forces: One CCG cutter vs a Philippine government fisheries vessel on a humanitarian mission.
battles.significance: Took place while ASEAN foreign ministers, including China's Wang Yi, met in Manila, underlining Beijing's refusal to ease pressure.

battles.name: Clash at Second Thomas Shoal
battles.place: Second Thomas Shoal (Ayungin), Spratly Islands, South China Sea
battles.outcome: Confrontation near the grounded BRP Sierra Madre; foreign ministers exchanged protests.
battles.forces: CCG personnel armed with batons vs Philippine Navy personnel.
battles.significance: Physical violence against Philippine service members is the kind of incident that could test the US-Philippine Mutual Defense Treaty.
